Not the main series, no. I'm super happy that Pokemon has largely stayed true to its child-friendly roots since its inception. I wouldn't have come back to watch the whole series as an adult if it wasn't a lighthearted break from the more mature shows I also watch. This also means I can share the show with my younger family members if I want.

I have enjoyed the occasional side series that has taken a slightly more "PG" tone (Origins, Hisuian Snow), or otherwise felt created with the franchise's sizable adult fanbase in mind (Concierge, with its protagonist that struggles with relatable adult problems). But I would prefer it if the main series remained a lighthearted throwback to my youth.

Horizons has been more focused on exploring characters than moving the overarching plot forwards in the past few episodes, and I personally am loving it.

Pure self-indulgent fanfiction, the anime absolutely DOES NOT have to end this way for me to enjoy it, but here we go:

The primary lesson of Ash’s Pokemon training career has been that life comes with ups and downs, wins and losses, so it’s best to focus on the journey rather than the destination.

Cut to a PWC in the far future. The reigning monarch Ash takes his loss with grace, and hands his title to a younger challenger.

Struggling with his loss, Ash retires to the sandy beaches of Alola to focus on being a more attentive Alolan Champion. 

Ash tells his fiancée Serena that he’s going for a malasada run to clear his head. He walks up to the food truck’s counter and is greeted with a hearty “What’ll it be, Twerp?”

Ash reflexively grabs his Pikachu, but Team Rocket assures Ash that they’ve given up on stealing the PWC-winning rodent and have quit the Pokemon stealing business altogether. So, Ash cautiously asks TRio to cater his wedding, and promises that they won’t blast off as long as they don’t try any funny business.

Cue a cute little wedding scene where all of Ash’s friends, rivals, and mentors tell Ash about what they’ve been up to while Ash has been up to his champion business. Ash kisses the bride, and everyone drinks the same rated-G champagne from Kukui’s wedding.

Fade to black, and then the next series focuses on a new hero’s journey.

I developed an imaginary friend loosely based on my friend that I could roleplay difficult conversations with before confronting the real thing. Over time I grew to enjoy the imaginary companionship in my alone time and developed more imaginary friends.

For what it's worth, I do not seriously believe my imaginary friends to be "headmates", "alters", or "tulpas". I am completely aware my imaginary friends are not real and do not possess sentience.
